intake_corrections: Five sequential intake stages omit iterative pseudo-label training, multiple backbones, snapshot/fold aggregation and training lifecycle.
Paper describes ResNet34 and ResNeXt50 encoders, concurrent spatial/channel excitation, feature pyramid attention and hypercolumns.
Paper specifies three rounds, initialization reset each round, pseudo-label-only training followed by labeled fine-tuning in later rounds, and final averaging of rounds two and three.
Pinned source uses binary Lovasz hinge, not a multiclass softmax loss. Keras flat hinge uses ELU plus one for sorted errors.
Depth-channel intake claim still requires comparison against actual preprocessing; do not assume it matches source.
source_script_findings: Keras first-stage training specifies five folds and successive 125,125,40,40,40 epoch calls; later stage specifies 40,40,125,20,20,25 epochs. These are not the uniform paper schedule.
PyTorch scripts select different Res34Unet variants across stages; training includes optional multi-head auxiliary losses.
PyTorch train_cv constructs a model before its five-fold loop and explicitly reloads per fold only for res34v5. Cross-fold initialization isolation for the other variants is not established.
PyTorch model forward calls functional dropout without training=self.training. Synthetic current-runtime probe confirms parent eval does not disable this pattern.
Best checkpoint uses state_dict without cloning. Synthetic current-runtime probe confirms the saved mapping changes with parameter updates.
RandomSampler is passed through shuffle. Current runtime treats it as truthy and constructs another sampler; this is not evidence of an immediate exception.
PyTorch depth channels are image, vertical unit ramp and their product; they do not consume measured depth metadata.
Keras ensemble weights reverse-ordered snapshots equally in stage one and 1,1,1,3 in later stages; branch blend is equal-weighted.
PyTorch ensemble scores are globally min-max normalized over the supplied query population; constant ranges divide by zero in source.
Constant-image suppression applies to the Keras branch only. Final masks use strict score above 0.5; confidence counts strict score below 0.2 or above 0.8.
Source pseudo-label selectors use confidence and predicted area conditions; these differ from the paper no-filtering recipe.
Final source script enables mosaic-based mask propagation postprocessing, which must be included in full workflow reconstruction.
